perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s available perspective:

- Sara knows she is a Speech-Language Pathologist and American Indian, working at a community health center. She knows Shirley Whiteplume is a nurse, long-time colleague, and close friend at the same center.
- Sara attended the funeral of a mutual patient. She observed Shirley appearing somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- At the funeral, Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and had seen how much Shirley cared. Shirley said it had been tough, she kept thinking if something more could have been done, and it was hard to let go. Sara replied they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought.
- During a coffee break, Sara raised the topic of treatment decisions, wanting to understand Shirley’s feelings and possibly ease her sense of responsibility. Shirley said she felt responsible, wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped, and said it was hard to accept. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone.
- In the office, Sara observed Shirley holding back feelings and being reserved/minimally expressive. Sara told her it was okay to be open. Shirley said she didn’t want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said expressing emotion doesn’t make someone weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she’d try.
- Later, Sara felt her previous confrontation may have been too harsh and apologized. Shirley said it was a bit much but knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley. Shirley thanked her and said talking helps.
- Later, Sara observed Shirley seemed improved and felt hopeful. Sara asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and suggested planning something for the weekend.
- Sara participated in all these conversations and actions. She has no access to Shirley’s private thoughts beyond what Shirley said or what Sara observed.
